public_rationale: Zitron said every major tech company selling AI is 'on some level' dependent on big tech's willingness to subsidize the industry. 'On some level' sets no bar, so almost any reliance counts and none can be ruled out. 'Subsidize' means selling below cost. In the same post he says hyperscalers hide these costs and 'we can't know for sure'. No public data shows big tech's AI costs against its prices. 'Every single one' also includes big tech itself, which makes the claim close to circular. The claim is a framing more than a checkable fact. Picking an earlier financial quarter to test it would replace his present-tense words with a period he did not name.
limitations: Some single cases, such as AI labs relying on hyperscaler investment and credits, may fit his description. They cannot test a claim about 'every single one' at an undefined level.

our_interpretation: 'These companies' refers to every major consumer and enterprise tech player selling an AI product and running compute on big tech's systems. The tense is present, so it describes the state of things around the post date (September 2024).

Checking the claim would require showing that big tech prices AI compute and models below cost (a subsidy), and that each company's AI offering depends on that. The speaker says in the same post that hyperscalers 'bake those costs into other parts of their earnings' and that 'we can't know for sure'. No public cost data shows below-cost pricing.
'On some level' sets no threshold for dependence. 'Every single one' includes big tech firms themselves, which makes the statement close to circular for them.
criteria.support_condition: None can be stated fairly. The claim would need public evidence of below-cost pricing by big tech plus dependence for every major AI seller, and 'on some level' gives no threshold.
criteria.contradiction_condition: None can be stated fairly. Showing that some company runs its own compute, or pays full price, would not rule out dependence 'on some level'.
